svg.title: Device and Pharma Dockets by the Dollar
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-07-device-pharma-dollar-stack; chapter number: 4; title: Device and Pharma Dockets by the Dollar; subtitle: Global deals, inventory settlements and bellwether verdicts; chart type: stacked_comparison; total range: From a $40 million PowerPort verdict to a $1.5 billion Bard hernia mesh deal; buckets: label: Bard hernia mesh global settlement; low: 1000000000; high: 1500000000; notes: About 38,000 cases (about 25,000 MDL plus about 13,000 Rhode Island); administration runs 2 to 3 years.; label: Abbott NEC inventory settlement; low: 675000000; high: 675000000; notes: Implies about $80,000 per case for about 2,000 cases beyond the $495 million Gill verdict.; label: Covidien Patterson bellwether verdict; low: 88000000; high: 88000000; notes: Covidien MDL near 2,500 cases, growing roughly 100 filings a month.; label: Bard PowerPort plaintiff verdict; low: 40000000; high: 40000000; notes: Followed by a record 400 filings in one month; total over 4,000.; caption: Every screen converges on a documented complication, a revision or removal surgery, and records naming the exact product.; assumptions note: There is no set payout; values vary by brand, injury severity and case details. Practitioners split on whether $80,000 NEC cases justify paid acquisition.; note: Sources: Joe Fantini on Case Works (oc04hOYvUBA) and Jon and Marc (2lQbSEVsxgE, P4L_OgCBmDc); Timothy O'Brien on Cut to the Chase Network (JlBWnsNpbyc); Drugwatch (y_Jf3JpGO8Y).
